sections.title: Visual System
sections.preamble: The application already carries a bright green ramp in its stylesheet. It is not applied consistently, five competing accent themes sit beside it, and the supporting material was drawn in a different palette entirely. This section makes one palette govern everything.

items.text: Adopt the bright green ramp as the only brand palette, across the application, the maps, the deck and every document
Retire the pine, sand, clay, indigo and plum accent themes, which dilute the brand and triple the visual QA surface
Remove the accent picker from the appearance screen and reduce it to light and dark
Publish the token set as the single source of truth: ramp, neutrals, status, radii, elevation, spacing
Replace every hard coded colour literal in components with a token reference
Define three named elevations and delete every one off shadow value
Define one spacing scale and remove every off scale margin and padding
Define a type scale with named roles and remove every one off font size
Select and self host one display typeface rather than relying on the system stack, which renders differently on every handset
Select and self host an Urdu typeface that sets Nastaliq correctly
Subset and preload both typefaces so the first paint does not shift
Normalise every icon to one family, one stroke weight and one grid size
Replace the mascot with a flat brand device, or remove it; in its present form it overlaps content on the home, committees, credit and account screens
Give the assistant a fixed entry point in the header rather than a floating character
Redraw the green header as a defined surface with a controlled edge rather than a slab carrying a stray lighter circle
Make the header treatment identical on every screen that uses one
Replace the blue credit score ring, which clashes with the brand, with the brand ramp
Stop the score ring being clipped by the header edge on the account screen
Replace the red outgoing arrows in the activity list, which read as errors, with a neutral treatment
Establish a status colour convention and document it: success, warning, failure, information
Define one card component with a fixed radius, padding, border and elevation, and route every surface through it
Stop nesting grey tiles inside white cards, which produces a muddy surface
Define one list row component with a title, an optional subtitle, an optional leading icon and an optional trailing control

Add a reduced motion preference and honour it in every transition

sections.title: Screens
sections.preamble: Every screen except Home is rebuilt to the standard of the JazzCash, Easypaisa and SadaPay applications, studied from their own store screenshots on 23 September 2026. The audit behind this section was made on 24 September 2026 by opening every screen of the running application at phone width: 28 screens, the five committee tabs, the sign-in and sign-up screens, and the 25 components that render inside them. Home is the one screen kept as it stands. Sign up and sign in are redesigned from nothing. Part C1 applies to every screen and is checked on each one as it is rebuilt; parts C3 and C4 are done first, because C3 is a legal exposure and C4 is a screen that does not open.

items.text: No bezels: no bordered or framed container around a section, and never a card inside a card. Surfaces are separated by fill and space

No rounded pill or badge shapes, under the standing design rule. Buttons, chips, filters and status labels use square or lightly rounded corners; status is an icon, a colour and a word. The component set built on 23 September uses pill buttons and pill badges and is corrected first
No emojis in any screen, share text or notification. The country flag in the number field is the one the app shows today; the API's document verification page carries two symbols

No playful or self-referential copy: the assistant's greeting lines, exclamation marks, the tab title "Committee savings, made rewarding", the sign-in slogan, and the error screen's "not a ledger one"
No over-explaining: at most one line of supporting text under a title. Every explanatory paragraph is cut, or moved behind a single How it works link

No list-of-rows navigation. A screen whose job is to send the member somewhere becomes an icon grid and cards, in the manner of the JazzCash and Easypaisa inner pages. Rows stay only where the content is itself a ledger: payments, members, turns
items.where: ProfilePage, SettingsPage, VerifyPage, ReferPage, FeesPage, AutoPayPage

items.text: No eyebrow labels above titles and no capitalised section labels; nine files carry them
items.where: AgreementGate, Appearance, CnicCapture, CollectionOrder, ExitSheet, JoinSheet, AuthPage, CommitteePage, CreateCirclePage

items.text: No stack of equal-weight panels. A screen opens with its one answer, then the evidence, then the actions. The committee's first tab stacks six panels
No decorative circles on any header, hero or band
No off-brand colour on a surface: the orange streak card, the blue status chip, the blue information rule

No raw undefined, NaN or null on screen. Seen on Rewards (Points NaN, Longest run undefined, NaN to go) and on the committee Safety tab (score undefined against every member). Every number and name passes through a guard
No segmented control that wraps to two lines; the committee tabs do
Row actions (Remove, Make default, Remind) open in a sheet from the row, instead of sitting as buttons under every row
No truncated title in a header; the committee name is cut to "Gulshan ..."
Every screen checked in dark mode as it is rebuilt, since the older stylesheets hard code white

Wire the ballot to an endpoint: lib/parchi.ts holds the whole commit and reveal ceremony, the seat constrained draw and the public verification, and no route calls any of it, so no circle has ever drawn its seats. sections.title: Interface Service Endpoints
sections.preamble: The 123 endpoints in seventeen route files, and the new ones the partnership needs.

subs.title: Endpoints to Remove
subs.preamble: Endpoints that implement withdrawn designs: the vault, investment of member money, deposits held, Halqa cover and passwords.

items.text: POST /api/auth/change-password: remove the endpoint and its handler; sign in is by PIN; there is no password
GET /api/committees/:id/deposits: remove the endpoint and its handler; no deposits are held from members
POST /api/committees/:id/deposits/:depositId/confirm: remove the endpoint and its handler; no deposits are held from members
POST /api/committees/:id/default-cover/:paymentId: remove the endpoint and its handler; there is no Halqa cover; takaful or insurance only (29 September)
POST /api/committees/:id/invest: remove the endpoint and its handler; Halqa invests no member money
POST /api/committees/:id/liquidate: remove the endpoint and its handler; Halqa invests no member money
GET /api/committees/:id/investments: remove the endpoint and its handler; Halqa invests no member money
GET /api/partner/committees/:id/guarantee-fund: remove the endpoint and its handler; there is no guarantee fund; takaful or insurance only
GET /api/risk/catalog: remove the endpoint and its handler; the investment catalogue goes with the schemes
POST /api/risk/portfolio/optimize: remove the endpoint and its handler; there is no portfolio to optimise
GET /api/risk/committee/:id/profit-plan: remove the endpoint and its handler; no profit is planned from member money
GET /api/schemes: remove the endpoint and its handler; Halqa invests no member money, so the catalogue of twenty investment products goes
GET /api/schemes/:id/projection: remove the endpoint and its handler; Halqa invests no member money, so the catalogue of twenty investment products goes
POST /api/schemes: remove the endpoint and its handler; Halqa invests no member money, so the catalogue of twenty investment products goes
PATCH /api/schemes/:id: remove the endpoint and its handler; Halqa invests no member money, so the catalogue of twenty investment products goes
DELETE /api/schemes/:id: remove the endpoint and its handler; Halqa invests no member money, so the catalogue of twenty investment products goes
GET /api/vault: remove the endpoint and its handler; the vault is withdrawn and savings move to the bank (D12)
POST /api/vault/allocation: remove the endpoint and its handler; the vault is withdrawn and savings move to the bank (D12)
POST /api/vault/toggle: remove the endpoint and its handler; the vault is withdrawn and savings move to the bank (D12)
POST /api/vault/auto-cover: remove the endpoint and its handler; the vault is withdrawn and savings move to the bank (D12)
POST /api/vault/tier: remove the endpoint and its handler; the vault is withdrawn and savings move to the bank (D12)
POST /api/vault/goal: remove the endpoint and its handler; the vault is withdrawn and savings move to the bank (D12)
POST /api/vault/deposit: remove the endpoint and its handler; the vault is withdrawn and savings move to the bank (D12)
POST /api/vault/withdraw: remove the endpoint and its handler; the vault is withdrawn and savings move to the bank (D12)
POST /api/committees/:id/payout: rework as a payout instruction to the bank, never a payment by Halqa
GET /api/exchange: rework the listing in points (D9)
POST /api/exchange: rework the listing in points (D9)
POST /api/exchange/:id/bid: rework the bid as an offer in points (D9)
POST /api/exchange/:id/bids/:bidId/accept: rework acceptance as a points transfer with host approval (D9)
POST /api/partner/kyc: rework as the bank's onboarding result received by signed webhook
POST /api/profile/passport: decision needed: the shareable credit passport and its public check, now that reporting runs through TASDEEQ or the bank
GET /api/profile/leads/summary: review: what it returns and who may see it
POST /api/protection/delinquency/run: restrict to the scheduler and named administrators
POST /api/rewards/record: remove: rewards are issued only by the server from events, never recorded by the client

sections.title: Tests
sections.preamble: Each business rule with its own test case, then the journeys a member takes from start to finish, the load the service must carry, and the attacks it must resist. Items 568 to 591 are broken down here by rule and by journey.

items.text: Test, fee: Rs 85 charged on a monthly instalment of Rs 10,000
Test, fee: Rs 85 charged on instalments of Rs 2,000 and of Rs 25,000, the fee flat whatever the size
Test, fee: the same fee for the first seat and the last seat
Test, fee: no charge of any kind for an early turn
Test, fee: Hyper: Rs 15 a day on Design 1 and on Design 2
Test, fee: PSP service fee of 1.5 per cent added only when a wallet or card is used
Test, fee: no PSP service fee on a debit under the bank's mandate
Test, fee: PSP service fee rounded to the paisa the way the PSP rounds
Test, fee: discount of 80 per cent for a guarantee cheque and 50 per cent for verified income, never stacked
Test, fee: points used against a fee never exceed the fee
Test, fee: points for paying on time never exceed half the fee on that instalment, Rs 42.50
Test, fee: the fee shown before payment equals the fee charged and the fee on the receipt
Test, fee: the fee schedule version is recorded with every charge
Test, fee: no fee is ever expressed as a rate except the PSP service fee
Test, split: contribution, takaful or insurance fee, the Rs 85 fee and any PSP service fee add up to the amount debited
Test, split: Hyper Design 1: Rs 300, Rs 135 and Rs 15 make Rs 450
Test, split: Hyper Design 2: Rs 333.33, Rs 151.67 and Rs 15 make Rs 500, with the thirds rounded so the circle balances over 26 days
Test, split: each part posted to its own ledger account in one transaction
Test, split: the ledger balances after every posting
Test, split: identity one: the pot equals the contribution multiplied by the number of rounds
Test, split: identity two: the roster equals collectors per period multiplied by the number of periods
Test, split: a configuration that breaks either identity is refused at creation
Test, split: a circle without takaful or insurance posts no such part
Test, seat eligibility: a real bureau record with a good score opens every seat, once TASDEEQ publishes its bands
Test, seat eligibility: no score counts as good until TASDEEQ publishes its bands, so a scored member stops at the middle seats
Test, seat eligibility: a mid score on a real record opens the middle seats only
Test, seat eligibility: a low score on a real record is held to the last seats
Test, seat eligibility: a record too thin to score opens the middle seats
Test, seat eligibility: no bureau record at all starts in the last seats
Test, seat eligibility: a low score on no record is not treated as a bad record
Test, seat eligibility: one clean committee, known or unknown, opens every seat where the record could not speak
Test, seat eligibility: a clean committee does not excuse a low score resting on a real record
Test, seat eligibility: security covering the pot, less the relaxation of ten per cent, opens every seat
Test, seat eligibility: security below the relaxation does not count
Test, seat eligibility: security sources combine, and the total is what is tested
Test, seat eligibility: security cannot buy past a low score on a real record
Test, seat eligibility: the last seats are the final three, never earlier than the second half of the circle
Test, seat eligibility: the middle seats are the second half of the circle
Test, seat eligibility: tiers scale to a circle of 20 in the same proportions
Test, seat eligibility: tenure alone no longer decides a seat: the blanket quarantine is gone
Test, seat eligibility: a host cannot open an early seat on a circle between strangers
Test, seat eligibility: on a known circle the host's invitation stands in the matrix's place, as the affordability tests do
Test, seat eligibility: tiers are checked at joining, at every turn listing and at every bid, through one engine
Test, seat eligibility: tiers are recalculated at the close of every committee, from the clean completions it records
Test, seat eligibility: the ballot places members only in seats their tier allows
Test, seat eligibility: the member is told why the seats above are closed and how to open them
Test, affordability: all instalments together within a third of verified income
Test, affordability: within 40 per cent including loans reported by TASDEEQ
Test, affordability: the weighted load and forward liability tests apply from the fourth committee
Test, affordability: the tests apply to circles between strangers and Hyper, not to known circles
Test, affordability: a refusal gives the reason and the amount that would fit
Test, affordability: income from the member's own transfers and from loans is excluded
Test, identity confidence: a name match of 0.90 or more passes
Test, identity confidence: a name match from 0.80 to 0.90 goes to a person
Test, identity confidence: a name match below 0.80 fails with the reason
Test, identity confidence: a face match is required at level 2 and above
Test, identity confidence: address and job checks raise the level as specified
Test, identity confidence: levels 1 to 3 set from the combined checks
Test, identity confidence: an expired CNIC lowers the level until it is renewed
Test, salary pattern: salary from one employer on about the same day each month is detected
Test, salary pattern: daily circles: Rs 1,000 or more on five days of every week for eight weeks passes
Test, salary pattern: four days in one week fails the daily test
Test, salary pattern: transfers from the member's own accounts are excluded
Test, salary pattern: loan disbursements are excluded
Test, salary pattern: the payday learned is used as the first debit date
Test, salary pattern: a late salary moves the first attempt to the day it arrives, before the 8th
Test, collection: methods tried in the order: bank mandate, saved card, approval, by hand
Test, collection: first attempt on the payday
Test, collection: a retry each morning after a failure, five attempts at most, all before the 8th
Test, collection: the second method tried once on the last attempt where the member has one
Test, collection: no late charge before the 8th
Test, collection: late charges of 2, 5 and 10 per cent after the 8th, as the delay grows
Test, collection: daily circles: 5, 10 and 15 per cent at 12, 36 and 60 hours
Test, collection: arrears recorded against the round, never as a negative balance held by Halqa
Test, collection: arrears taken from the member's own pot on their turn
Test, collection: a debit never exceeds the mandate ceiling of one instalment
Test, collection: a cancelled mandate is never debited
Test, collection: cancelling a mandate moves the member to approval or payment by hand
Test, collection: a retried job never debits twice
Test, collection: a member without a partner bank account stays on approval and payment by hand
Test, collection: Hyper collects only by mandate or saved card
Test, collection: a partial payment is recorded and the balance stays due
Test, collection: payment by a verified family member is recorded as such
Test, collection: an advance payment is accepted and applied to the next instalment
Test, payout: the pot paid to the collector's verified account on the 8th, the same day
Test, payout: the account title checked before every payout
Test, payout: a payout to another bank goes by interbank transfer
Test, payout: a payout to a wallet that would exceed its monthly limit goes to the bank account instead
Test, payout: payouts paused on a circle with an open reconciliation break
Test, payout: a shortfall from a late member explained on the payout, with the takaful or insurance claim where it applies
Test, payout: the payout receipt matches the ledger to the paisa
Test, payout: a payout account changed in the last two hours is refused
Test, reconciliation: every ledger entry matched to one bank entry
Test, reconciliation: an unmatched entry becomes a break and pauses payouts on its circle
Test, reconciliation: a duplicate bank entry is detected
Test, reconciliation: a partial match is held for review
Test, reconciliation: a break resolved with a reason releases the pause
Test, reconciliation: the daily statement is ingested once even if delivered twice
Test, points: one point equals one rupee in every calculation
Test, points: the ledger is append only; no entry is edited or deleted
Test, points: no route exists from points to cash
Test, points: points move between members only as the price of a turn
Test, points: points are frozen while a member is in default
Test, points: purchases stay within the daily and monthly limits agreed with the bank
Test, points: members on Raqami cannot buy points
Test, points: unused points lapse only under the rule stated before purchase
Test, points: a returned order credits its points back
Test, points: the end of circle reward equals the profit on the member's balance, converted at one point a rupee
Test, turn market: a price above 100 per cent of the pot is refused
Test, turn market: a buyer whose band does not allow the earlier turn is refused
Test, turn market: forward liability and affordability are checked again for the buyer
Test, turn market: no trade settles without the host's approval
Test, turn market: settlement swaps the turns, moves the points and charges the fee in one transaction
Test, turn market: a cooling off period runs before settlement
Test, turn market: a trade is cancelled if either member defaults before settlement
Test, turn market: no trade is possible in Hyper or asset circles
Test, turn market: the maximum number of trades per member per circle is enforced
Test, turn market: a trade between linked accounts is refused
Test, recovery: the steps run in order, each only if the one before fails
Test, recovery: at step two the account is restricted and the score falls by 200
Test, recovery: at step three the operator is notified of the claim; Halqa pays nothing itself
Test, recovery: no step contacts a relative or a contact of the member
Test, recovery: a hardship plan pauses the ladder until its date
Test, recovery: a cure clears the restriction and records the recovery
Test, leaving a circle: each rung shows its arithmetic before the member confirms
Test, leaving a circle: restitution owed is calculated to the paisa

subs.title: Mobile Application Security
subs.preamble: OWASP MASVS v2.1: 24 controls in eight groups. Controls already held by an item elsewhere are met through it: identity images at rest (549), forced updates (644), pinning, rooted devices and device binding (812), and the transaction PIN (section AB).

items.text: Meet MASVS-STORAGE-1: the application stores sensitive data securely: tokens, PIN material and CNIC images only in the platform's secure storage, never in plain local storage
Meet MASVS-STORAGE-2: the application prevents leakage of sensitive data: no personal data in logs, screenshots of the task switcher, backups or the clipboard
Meet MASVS-CRYPTO-1: current strong cryptography used as intended: no home made schemes, no weak hashes for PINs
Meet MASVS-CRYPTO-2: keys managed to best practice: generated in the platform key store, never in the code
Meet MASVS-AUTH-1: secure authentication and authorisation with the interface service: short lived tokens, rotation, server side revocation
Meet MASVS-AUTH-2: local authentication done securely: biometric unlock bound to a key in the secure enclave
Meet MASVS-AUTH-3: sensitive operations secured with additional authentication: the transaction PIN
Meet MASVS-NETWORK-1: all network traffic secured to current practice: TLS 1.2 or later only
Meet MASVS-NETWORK-2: identity pinning for Halqa's own endpoints
Meet MASVS-PLATFORM-1: inter process communication used securely: deep links validated before acting
Meet MASVS-PLATFORM-2: web views used securely: no file access, no script bridges to untrusted content
Meet MASVS-PLATFORM-3: the user interface used securely: sensitive fields masked, overlays detected on payment screens
Meet MASVS-CODE-1: an up to date platform version required
Meet MASVS-CODE-2: a mechanism to enforce updates for a critical fix
Meet MASVS-CODE-3: only components without known vulnerabilities
Meet MASVS-CODE-4: all untrusted input validated and sanitised, including deep link parameters and QR contents
Meet MASVS-RESILIENCE-1: the integrity of the platform validated: rooted and jailbroken devices detected
Meet MASVS-RESILIENCE-2: anti tampering: the application's own integrity checked
Meet MASVS-RESILIENCE-3: anti static analysis: code obfuscated in release builds
Meet MASVS-RESILIENCE-4: anti dynamic analysis: debuggers and hooking frameworks detected before financial actions
Meet MASVS-PRIVACY-1: access to sensitive data and resources minimised: camera only for capture, no contacts or photos
Meet MASVS-PRIVACY-2: the member is not identified across services: no advertising identifiers
Meet MASVS-PRIVACY-3: transparency about data collection and use, in the application and the store listings
Meet MASVS-PRIVACY-4: the member controls their data: export, correction, consent withdrawal and deletion

subs.title: WCAG 2.2 Success Criteria
subs.preamble: Every success criterion at levels A and AA, as it applies to Halqa; items 607 to 614 broken down by criterion.

items.text: Meet WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non text Content: every icon, image and chart has a text alternative or is marked decorative
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.2.1 Audio only and Video only (Prerecorded): any explainer video carries a transcript
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded): videos captioned in English and Urdu
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative: videos described in text
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.2.4 Captions (Live): not used: no live media; recorded as not applicable
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded): videos carry audio description where they show what is not said
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: headings, lists and tables marked up as such
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence: reading order follows the visual order in both languages
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics: no instruction relies on shape, colour or position alone
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.3.4 Orientation: every screen works in portrait and landscape
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose: personal fields carry autocomplete purposes
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 Use of Color: paid, late and failed shown by a word and an icon as well as colour
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.2 Audio Control: no sound plays on its own
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum): text contrast at least 4.5 to 1, large text 3 to 1
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.4 Resize Text: text enlarges to 200 per cent without loss
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.5 Images of Text: no text set as an image, except logos
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.10 Reflow: no sideways scrolling at 320 pixels wide
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.11 Non text Contrast: controls, focus rings and chart marks at 3 to 1
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.12 Text Spacing: layouts hold when spacing is increased
Meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: tooltips can be dismissed and stay while pointed at
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.1.1 Keyboard: every function works from a keyboard on the web
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap: focus never trapped, sheets and dialogs included
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts: no single key shortcuts, or they can be switched off
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable: time limits such as the code and the session can be extended, security limits apart
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide: moving content such as carousels can be paused
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold: nothing flashes
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks: a skip link on the web
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.4.2 Page Titled: every screen has a title that says where the member is
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.4.3 Focus Order: focus moves in a meaningful order
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context): every link says where it goes
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.4.5 Multiple Ways: screens reachable by navigation and by search
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.4.6 Headings and Labels: headings and labels describe their content
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.4.7 Focus Visible: a visible focus state on every control
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum): the focused control never hidden by the tab bar or a sheet
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures: no gesture needs more than one finger or a path
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation: actions fire on release and can be abandoned
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.5.3 Label in Name: the spoken name contains the visible label
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.5.4 Motion Actuation: nothing triggered by shaking or tilting
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: ordering turns by dragging also possible by buttons
Meet WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum): targets at least 24 by 24 pixels, 44 where possible
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.1.1 Language of Page: the language of each screen declared
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.1.2 Language of Parts: Urdu passages inside English screens declared as Urdu
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.2.1 On Focus: focus never changes the screen on its own
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.2.2 On Input: choosing an option never submits by surprise
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation: navigation the same on every screen
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.2.4 Consistent Identification: the same control looks and is named the same everywhere
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.2.6 Consistent Help: help in the same place on every screen
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.3.1 Error Identification: errors named in text beside the field
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions: every field labelled
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.3.3 Error Suggestion: each error says how to fix it
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data): every payment, signature and closure reviewable and confirmable
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.3.7 Redundant Entry: nothing asked twice in one journey
Meet WCAG 2.2 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum): sign in without a memory test beyond the PIN, with biometric and paste of codes allowed
Meet WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: custom controls expose their name, role and state
Meet WCAG 2.2 4.1.3 Status Messages: payment results and errors announced to screen readers

sections.title: Features Measured against Other Finance Applications
sections.preamble: Features of Easypaisa, JazzCash, SadaPay, NayaPay, Raqami, Mashreq NEO, Money Fellows, Hakbah, Esusu, Revolut and Monzo already planned elsewhere: the help centre (item 327), the service status page (523), device management (551), the statement as a file (166), receipts shared as a file (284), Urdu throughout (595), limits set by the score (916), cashback as the end of circle reward (861), host tools (266 to 278), payment by any debit card or wallet (389), scheduled payments by mandate and saved card (390, 832), fingerprint verification in the bank's onboarding (744), savings between payday and the 8th (447), the transaction PIN, device cooling off, security advice and the Raast QR code (section AB), dark mode and search on every list (section AC), and reminders before the 8th (section AH). The invitation QR code, biometric unlock, the limits page, the notification centre and referral codes are built. The items below hold only what is new.

items.text: Application locked when it goes to the background, as banking applications do
A person behind the assistant in support chat, as the wallets offer
Circles between strangers released on a weekly schedule, as Hakbah releases its circles each Monday
Low data mode for slow connections
Home screen widget with the next due date, in the native build
Link to the member's Raast ID at the bank, as Easypaisa and SadaPay show it
Links to the bank's saving pots after a circle ends, as Raqami offers them
Links to the bank's card controls: virtual card and card freeze
Cash deposit points shown for members paid in cash: Askari Bank branches for Raqami, the bank's branches for Mashreq
Request money from a member by request to pay: for the chairman's decision; useful to hosts, but a source of pressure on members
Rent payments reported to bureaus, as Esusu does: recommended for exclusion, since it lies outside the committee product; for the chairman's decision
Spending insights, as Revolut and Monzo show: recommended for exclusion, since the bank holds the account; for the chairman's decision
Round ups into savings: recommended for exclusion as the bank's product; for the chairman's decision
Mini applications inside the wallet, as Easypaisa and JazzCash run: recommended for exclusion, since they lie outside the committee product; for the chairman's decision
Banking over WhatsApp: recommended for exclusion, since Halqa sends notices on WhatsApp and takes no instructions there; for the chairman's decision

Price by slot, with fees on early slots and discounts on late ones, as Money Fellows charges: excluded, since the fee is the same for every seat (30 September) and the turn market serves members who want an earlier turn
Prepaid card for payouts, as Money Fellows issues: excluded, since payouts go to the member's bank account (D2)
Small loans offered inside wallets: excluded, since Halqa offers no loans
Buy now pay later: excluded, since Halqa offers no loans

sections.title: Eligibility, Security, Host Pay and Speed
sections.preamble: The chairman's ruling of 5 October 2026. Most members are working adults, so waiting is designed out; what remains is a test of whether the pot is recoverable, by history or by security.

subs.title: Income without the Wait
subs.preamble: The two month observation stops being the normal route (5 October). Items 396, 471 and 962 are rewritten in place.

items.text: Remove the two month wait as the normal route into a circle between strangers: documentary proof verifies on the same day, and the observation of two salary credits (MIN_MONTHS in the salary pattern engine) is kept only as the fallback for a member with no document and no history at the partner bank (5 October)
Payslip, statement and the partner bank's own statement data (D10) each verify income immediately, with no waiting period
Joining screens state which proof verifies at once and which route needs observation, so no member is left waiting without knowing why
Members are assumed to be working adults aged 18 or over; no screen implies that unemployment is expected (5 October)
Measure how many members verify by document against how many fall to observation, and report it monthly; if the fallback is common the assumption behind this ruling is wrong
Exceptional case path: a member with no document and no history is told the wait, its length and what ends it, and is offered the security route instead

subs.title: Seat Eligibility
subs.preamble: The blanket quarantine of items 475 and 920 is replaced by a matrix of real bureau history and score.

items.text: Remove the blanket quarantine that holds every new member to the last seats whatever their score, and replace it with the matrix below (5 October)
Clean circles required before the first positions open reduced from two to one (REQUIRED_CLEAN_CIRCLES)
Manual verification by telephone removed as a condition of early turns, since it cannot scale to 100,000 members
Seat eligibility: a member who has real, substantial bureau history and a good score may take any seat
Seat eligibility: a member who has a mid score may take the middle seats
Seat eligibility: a member who has a low score may take the last seats
Seat eligibility: a member who has a record too thin to score properly may take the middle seats, and the first positions after one clean circle, known or unknown
Seat eligibility: a member who has no credit history at all, so no or very limited score factors may take the last seats, and any seat after one clean circle, known or unknown

A member with no bureau record is distinguished in code from a member with a thin record and from a member with a genuinely low score; the three carry different seat rights and must not collapse into one band
No score counts as good until TASDEEQ publishes its band cutoffs, so the band gate stays provisional and every member falls to the thin or absent history rows (chairman, 5 October)
Remove the spawn score of 700, which reads as a good band and would defeat the ruling above; a member with no history carries no score at all until one is earned or read from the bureau
Recalibrate the cutoffs in one place once TASDEEQ's bands arrive, as the engine already allows
A clean circle is defined in code: every instalment paid, no late charge outstanding, no default after collection, the circle closed
The seat map shows which seats are open to the member and the reason the others are closed, with the route to open them
Tests for every row of the matrix, including the move from thin history to any seat after one clean circle

subs.title: Security in Place of Credit History
subs.preamble: Where the pot is recoverable from security the member holds, no credit history is required. The money stays in the member's own account, held by the bank, and earns the bank's profit throughout.

items.text: Security route: a member needs no credit history where the pot is recoverable from security they hold (5 October)
Security accepted: enrolment in an asset committee whose dates and pot align with the circle
Security accepted: points, which may be bought with money
Security accepted: money of roughly the same amount in the member's savings account at the partner bank
Sources combine: points, savings and an asset committee are added together and tested against the pot
Relaxation of 10 per cent: security counts as sufficient at 90 per cent of the pot or more, in every case (5 October)
The member signs a clause not to withdraw the money for the circle's duration
The bank places the hold on the member's own account; Halqa never holds the money, so the no custody position stands (5 October)
Held money sits in the partner bank's savings product and earns its profit for the member throughout the lock, so giving security costs the member nothing (chairman, 5 October: not too harsh)
The savings product used for security is the same one that holds instalments between payday and the 8th (D12), so the bank needs no second product
Profit earned on held security shown to the member during the circle
The hold is released the moment the member's last instalment is paid, automatically
The security route does NOT open the gate for a member whose score is low on substantial, real credit factors; security cannot buy past a known bad record (5 October)
An asset committee offered as security must align with the circle's dates and pot, so the member cannot collect and run (5 October)
Security is rechecked when a member trades for an earlier turn, since the pot at risk changes
Points pledged as security are frozen in the points ledger and cannot be spent or transferred
Counsel on the hold: whether a bank lien over a member's own savings is enforceable in Pakistan and what the member must sign for it
Shariah view on holding a member's savings as security for a committee, for the Islamic window
Tests: security short by 9 per cent passes, short by 11 per cent fails, and a combination of sources is added correctly

subs.title: Host Commission
subs.preamble: Ten per cent of the profit the circle made for Halqa, paid when the circle closes.

items.text: Host commission: 10 per cent of the profit the circle made for Halqa, not of its revenue, paid at the end of each circle (5 October)

Profit of a circle defined in code: Halqa's share of the fees actually collected, less the running cost of each payment taken, less points and fee waivers issued on that circle at 1 point = Rs 1, less anything Halqa itself bore on a default
Commission floored at zero: a circle that made Halqa nothing pays the host nothing, and no commission is ever negative
Commission calculated only when the circle closes with every member collected and no arrears open
The host chooses points or cash; cash is paid by the bank to the host's account, points through the points ledger at 1 point = Rs 1 (5 October)
Worked example shown to the host before they create a circle: on 12 members at Rs 10,000 a month the circle earns Halqa about Rs 7,200 and the host about Rs 720
Running estimate of the commission shown during the circle, marked as an estimate
Commission statement for the host: fees collected, costs deducted, profit and the 10 per cent
Commission recorded as a cost of the circle in the business model, so the Rs 50 contribution a member a month is restated net of it
Tax treatment of a host's commission confirmed, and withholding applied if it is due
Commission terms in the host agreement, including that it is discretionary on a circle that ends early
A host may not take commission on a circle in which they themselves defaulted
Controls against a host creating circles of friends purely to earn commission: limits per host and a review of circles that fail early
Tests for the profit formula at a clean circle, a circle with a default and a circle with heavy points issuance
To create a circle a member needs one of: a good score with substantial proof; two clean known committees; or the security of AQ3 (5 October)
Remove the hosting gate of a score of 700 or more, which cannot stand while no score counts as good
The host route is shown to a member who does not yet qualify, with what is missing
Security pledged to qualify as a host is tested against the pot of the circle being created, with the same 10 per cent relaxation
Tests for each of the three host routes, and for refusal when none is met

subs.title: Ten Minutes to an Account
subs.preamble: The chairman's limit, and the measurement that shows the journey does not meet it today.

items.text: Account opening must complete in under ten minutes, measured from the welcome screen to a verified account (chairman, 5 October)
MEASURED 5 OCTOBER: twenty one screens stand between the welcome screen and a verified account, which does not fit ten minutes even when nothing goes wrong. The steps below are the budget that does
Time budget, Welcome: 5 seconds (keep)
Time budget, Phone number: 20 seconds (keep)
Time budget, One time code: 25 seconds (keep; autofill the code)
Time budget, PIN set and confirmed: 25 seconds (keep; one screen with two steps)
Time budget, Name and date of birth: 40 seconds (keep; read both from the CNIC where the capture succeeds)
Time budget, Address and city: 50 seconds (keep, since the bank needs it to open the account)
Time budget, CNIC front, back and review: 90 seconds (keep; read the fields rather than ask them again)
Time budget, Liveness: 45 seconds (keep)
Time budget, Identity check: 45 seconds (keep; show progress, never a blank wait)
Time budget, Bank account opening and the biometric check: 180 seconds (the bank's own journey; the longest step and not Halqa's to shorten)
Time budget, Biometric unlock offer: 10 seconds (keep; one tap, skippable)
Move Occupation and employer off account opening and into joining a circle, since it is not needed to hold an account
Move Income declaration off account opening and into joining a circle, since it is not needed to hold an account
Move Income verification upload off account opening and into joining a circle between strangers, since it is not needed to hold an account
Move Income verification status off account opening and into joining a circle between strangers, since it is not needed to hold an account
Move Verification levels off account opening and into an explanation reached from the account screen, since it is not needed to hold an account
Move Bureau instruction off account opening and into joining a circle between strangers, since it is not needed to hold an account
Move Bureau instruction confirmation off account opening and into joining a circle between strangers, since it is not needed to hold an account
Move Adverse action disclosure off account opening and into the refusal it belongs to, since it is not needed to hold an account
Total budget of the steps above is 535 seconds, just under nine minutes, leaving a minute for the member to think; any new step on this path must take time from another
Time to open an account measured in the application and reported, with the slowest step named
Alert when the median time to open an account passes eight minutes
Fields read from the CNIC rather than typed again: name, date of birth, CNIC number and expiry
Every screen on the path loads in under one second on a low end handset over a third generation connection
The bank's own account opening journey timed with the bank, and shortened where the bank allows
A member who abandons the journey resumes where they left off, with nothing typed twice
End to end test that walks the whole path and fails if it exceeds ten minutes of scripted interaction
